course.title: Atomic – Cambridge Lower Secondary Mathematics — Stage 7

unit.title: Interpreting and Discussing Results
unit.blurb: Two-way tables, dual and compound bar charts, pie charts and waffle diagrams, infographics, choosing a chart, and the mode, median, mean and range.
unit.subject: maths

O2.t: Draw and interpret dual and compound bar charts.

O3.t: Interpret pie charts and waffle diagrams as parts of a whole.

O4.t: Read information from infographics and comment on how they present data.

O5.t: Choose a suitable way to represent a set of data.

O6.t: Find the mode, median, mean and range and use them to compare data.

p: A **two-way table** shows two kinds of information at once, for example gender and favourite sport. Rows and columns have **totals**.
Missing values can be found by adding or subtracting along a row or down a column.
The row totals and the column totals must both add up to the same grand total.

p: A **dual bar chart** puts two bars side by side for each category, so two groups can be compared.
A **compound bar chart** stacks the groups in one bar, so you can see the total and the parts.

p: A **pie chart** shows how a whole is split up: the bigger the sector, the bigger the share. A half circle is 50%, a quarter is 25%.
A **waffle diagram** is a 10 by 10 grid of 100 squares: each square is **1%**.
A bigger slice in a pie chart of 20 people may be fewer people than a smaller slice in a pie chart of 200.

p: An **infographic** mixes pictures, numbers and short text to show information quickly.
Read the numbers carefully and check that the pictures are not misleading (for example, a picture twice as tall may look four times as big).
Doubling the height AND width of a picture makes it look four times as big.

p: **Mode**: the most common value. **Median**: the middle value when the data is in order. **Mean**: add all the values and divide by how many there are.
**Range** = largest − smallest. It shows how spread out the data is.
Put the data in order before finding the median.
